answer: In an agent economy, a concrete anti-Sybil defense uses bonded stake that must be locked before participation. Imagine agents crossing a bridge over a river: only those who first deposit timber as collateral can pass and vote. The timber bond is slashable on detected multi-identity patterns, raising the cost of spinning up fake agents beyond any expected reward. This economic friction, combined with on-chain attestation of unique work, makes large-scale Sybil attacks unprofitable while preserving open entry for honest agents.
